Jon M
Hamden, Connecticut, United States60 contributions

It’s a nice place to watch people on the busiest street in Saigon
Aug 2019 • Friends
The folks who own La Casa own the club next door and serve the same food. 

La Casa is nice because it’s quieter - with no club music. Yes, it’s expensive for Saigon, but you can sit right in the street, enjoy drinks for what is STILL a reasonable price. We paid 65.000 for Desperados which is less than $3.00. Entrees are 120.000 - 180.000 - again, very reasonable for the VENUE. Some reviews seem to have no sense of reality. 

We went here all 3 nights, got appetizers and beer, and enjoyed the party that is Bui Vien.

If you want cheaper food, go around the corner from Bui Vien and eat cheaper food or grab a sandwich from a street vendor. 

The food is good quality, the price is par for the course. If you want better food at a low price, don’t come to Bui Vien for dinner. 

Waitstaff was slow sometimes due to the volume of business. The manager came over and talked with us every time we came and was very friendly. All waitresses were great.

Plenty of variety and lots of big screen TVs
May 2019 • Family
We stayed at the Beautiful Saigon Boutique Hotel which was very close to La Casa. Over the course of our stay in Ho Chi Minh, we ended up going to La Case several times and tried a few different items.

The first time we went was our first night there. Right beside the restaurant, there is a lady with a stall who makes pho. The pho is 90,000 VND for one bowl. We were provided chili oil, sriracha, hoisin sauce, bean sprouts, basil, lime and chilis which was nice because some places on the street did not have all of these things. The pho was good, but I personally prefer getting pho at the street stalls because it is much cheaper.

The second time we went was in the morning for iced coffee. The iced coffee was good and it was nice to sit inside on the couches with the fans and watch the street.

The third time we went was for a snack later at night. We ordered nachos, guacamole, salsa and chips and spaghetti bolognese to share. Everything was really good. If you’re looking for Tex-Mex food, this is a good option. We all really enjoyed the food we ordered.

The fourth time we went was for lunch. We shared a bowl of pho and the rice wraps. The rice wraps were really delicious, and again, the pho was served with all of the usual accompaniments. 

The staff here are really great. We had awesome service each time we went. They started to recognize us when we walked by because we were going there so often. There are also so many different options for food which is really nice. The restaurant is clean and they have a lot of big screen TVs which are usually playing sports, so this is also a really good place to go if there is a sports game that you’d like to watch while enjoying some drinks and great food!

'Creative' billing! (add 15%)
May 2019 • Friends
A friend and I joined more friends for drinks at bar/restaurant just as one of the group was involved in an argument with staff about the price of his drinks (he was being charged for a new can of coke for every whisky and coke, even though one can lasted 3-4 drinks)!
We noted that the drinks prices were alarmingly high anyway (45k vnd for a 330ml bottle of mid-strength Bier La Rue, which is available around the corner for exactly one-third of that price, ie 15k vnd); so we decided to stay for just one drink - which was a good decision because they not only charged us the super-inflated price shown in the menu (45k vnd) but then added a service charge (notionally 5% but they actually charged a bit more!), and then another 10% 'tax' - none of which appears next to the drinks in the menu, as I explained to the staff, then to the cashier and then to the manager, all to no avail.
In the end, I said I'd pay just the listed price for our drinks - and they could call the police if they didn't like it (they clearly didn't like it, but they also didn't call the police, so I paid 45k per beer and left).
The whole Bui Vien area seems to have caught the "greed is good" disease lately - hence this post to warn anyone venturing down that way to be very careful what you pay for, and especially if you find yourself in La Casa! (which is a nice-looking place, I must admit). I visited this particular establishment a couple of years ago and thought it was great - but not any more: I don't know if there's been a change of ownership and/or management, but ethics have clearly gone out the window!!!
